target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
Both disclosures define the composition of Financial and Non-Financial Risk Management functions, their independence from business units, and their respective reporting lines to the Chief Risk Officer and Head of Non-Financial Risk. The 2025 text (ms_2025_7_P157_S001) aligns with the 2024 text (ms_2024_7_P265_S001) on this structural definition, despite the 2025 version adding specific function names (e.g., Climate Risk).

Both disclosures describe how the independent risk functions assist senior management (and the FRC/BRC) in monitoring and controlling risk through control processes and maintain their own risk governance structures. The 2025 text (ms_2025_7_P157_S002, S003) matches the 2024 text (ms_2024_7_P265_S002, S003) on these operational roles and governance aspects.

comparisons.peer_topic: Three lines of defense governance structure
comparisons.peer_summary: The company manages risk across three lines of defense: Front Line Units (FLUs), Global Risk Management (GRM), and Corporate Audit, with control functions such as Legal and Global Human Resources operating outside these lines, all integrated into the management-level governance structure.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and BAC describe integrated governance structures for risk management, though they use different structural models. MS emphasizes that independent risk functions 'maintain its own risk governance structure with specified individuals and committees responsible for aspects of managing risk.' BAC similarly states that its risk management lines of defense are 'integrated into our management-level governance structure,' where control functions operate alongside Front Line Units and Global Risk Management. While MS focuses on the independence and internal governance of specific risk functions, BAC focuses on the integration of risk lines (FLU, GRM, Audit) into the broader management governance.

sentences.text: Each function maintains its own risk governance structure with specified individuals and committees responsible for aspects of managing risk.
We have clear ownership and accountability for managing risk across three lines of defense: Front Line Units (FLUs), GRM and Corporate Audit.
The three lines of defense are integrated into our management-level governance structure.

comparisons.peer_topic: Risk Governance Structure and Escalation Channels
comparisons.peer_summary: The Independent Risk Management (IRM) function maintains its independence through a risk governance and oversight structure that provides specific channels for escalating risks and issues to senior management, the Firm Risk Committee (FRC), and the Board of Directors. This structure includes a chart illustrating principal standing committees of the Board and key senior management committees, though it notes that additional committees and escalation channels exist beyond those shown.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM disclose that their independent risk management functions maintain specific governance and oversight structures to support risk monitoring and control. MS states that these independent functions 'assist senior management and the FRC in monitoring and controlling our risk' through control processes and maintain their own governance structures. Similarly, JPM describes a risk governance and oversight structure that 'provides channels for the escalation of risks and issues to senior management, the FRC and the Board of Directors' to support the independence of the IRM function. Both entities explicitly mention the Firm/Financial Risk Committee (FRC) as a key body in this governance structure.

sentences.text: These functions assist senior management and the FRC in monitoring and controlling our risk through a number of control processes.
Each function maintains its own risk governance structure with specified individuals and committees responsible for aspects of managing risk.

The independent status of the IRM function is supported by a risk governance and oversight structure that provides channels for the escalation of risks and issues to senior management, the FRC and the Board of Directors, as appropriate.
